blindSummary:
Self-governing territory of a distant metropolitan state: same-sex marriage legal since 2017 (later than the metropolitan state itself); small, church-centred but safe society.

Underlying evidence base is that of the metropolitan state, adapted for local conditions.
blindOutOfScope: Territory of a distant metropolitan state; local deviations noted.
blindSourceSummaries: Independent newsroom report (Sept 2024) on the metropolitan state's decade of self-ID legal gender recognition - included as regional context because this territory forms part of that state; the self-ID framework and its low-conflict implementation provide the relevant background.

International LGBT-rights organisation country overview for the metropolitan state (updated March 2026), included because this territory forms part of that state: robust protections, self-determined gender markers, 'X' passports, SOGIESC discrimination protections. (The territory has its own legislation, with self-ID-style recognition adopted there in 2017.)

LGBTQ+ news outlet (Nov 2006): campaign coverage under the message that homophobia was 'perfectly legal' here - LGBT activists gathered ~20,000 signatures demanding anti-discrimination protection and a registered-partnership law to match the surrounding countries; documents that violence and discrimination against out gay people were 'not uncommon', with no legal protection.

LGBTQ+ news outlet (Sept 2010): a member of this territory's parliament from an agrarian-centrist party refused to attend a state banquet for the gay prime minister of a neighbouring state and her wife, calling the visit 'a direct provocation' - the incident sparked controversy in both countries.
Religion-and-current-affairs site (Sept 2010): coverage of the same parliamentarian's snub of the neighbouring state's gay leader - illustrating the religious-political context of this territory.

A neighbouring state's LGBT news site (July 2015): a prominent local singer responded to the parliamentarian's demand to ban Pride festivals (held two days before the national holiday) - publicly urging that such 'narrow-minded opinions' be ignored; documents ongoing anti-Pride politics in the territory.
